1.1: Concerning what Meqabis did unto the Jews in Mesopotamia of Syria: and he slew them, with all those of them, unto the environs of Jerusalem — from Iyaboq and from Ṭəfʿa — unto the holy precinct.
1.2: For they marched forth from Samaria unto the environs of Jerusalem, and all its villages; and they slew with the edge of the sword, until there remained not save one; for the Edomites joined — and the Syrians, and the Amalekites — with Meqabis the Moabite, who destroyed the city of Jerusalem.
1.3: And when the children of Israel rebelled, Meqabis the Moabite sent unto them, and slew them — all of them — with a slaughter.
1.4: And concerning this thing, the wrath of God went up against His holy city; and they arrayed themselves in their camp.
1.5: And the Edomites marched forth, and the Elofəli; and they seized [them], to take vengeance, [upon] the city of God — for of His own will He sent them, because they transgressed the word of God.
1.6: But Meqabis — his city was Remat of Moab — rose up mightily from his city, and arrayed himself with those that were with him.
1.7: And there gathered all the multitudes of Mesopotamia unto Syria, that they might destroy the city of God. And from thence he summoned the Elofəlawəyan and the Amalekites, and gave them much gold and silver, and horses and chariots, that they might be with him in the camp.
1.8: And they came together, and besieged the city; and they poured out their blood like water — of those who dwelt therein.
1.9: And they forgot Jerusalem — like — and he wrought therein filth and refuse, and all that pleaseth not God; by the doing of they defiled the city of God, which was full of righteousness and holiness.
1.10: And they left their slain — O Thou that doest — as food for the birds of heaven, and their flesh — O Thy righteous — for the beasts of the desert.
1.11: And they were shut in, the multitudes; and the pangs of death — and as for our enemies, they brought forth that which was in the belly, until God shall have mercy — [God] who trieth the heart and the kidneys — for those without the fear of God did as Satan taught them.
1.12: And they repented in their streets, while they rejoiced because of the evil which they had done against the people of God; and He took away grace and mercy which I shewed, from the holy city.
1.13: And when they entered and returned into their dwellings, they made joy, and rejoicing, and encampment.

2.9: And at that time Meqabis wept before God because of his sin, and put on ashes; for God had mercy.
2.10: And he declared that God will not turn aside the evil which He spoke by the mouth of His prophet; for His eyes are open and slumber not, and His ears are uncovered and are not deaf, and not the word which He spoke; and He shall perform it in one moment, in the twinkling of an eye.
2.11: And he rent his garments, and put on sackcloth, and cast ashes upon his head; and he wept and cried out before the Lord his God, because of the evil which he had done.

3.11: And at that time he went forth from and bowed down unto the prophet, while he said thus — and thus: "May God cause me to inherit — that it depart not from thee — but cause me to inherit that which thou commandest; for I have spurned God, and have not walked in His commandment as my fathers; for we have no law, but it was shewn unto us that we should worship idols, as our fathers taught us."
3.12: "But as for me, I did not hearken unto the voice of His prophets of God until now; for I have sinned — I who walked in my sins, and in the pride of my heart, and in the lifting up of my neck — wherein I spurned the commandment of God, and walked not in His statutes, and him which he commanded me.

5.11: And there is none over them — all — who loveth God their Maker.
5.12: And again they worship idols whose name is Baal Peor, and worship him, and believe in him as God their Maker; for deaf and dumb is he, and there is none who seeth and who heareth, for a graven image, the work of the hand of man, is he — which the craftsman forged of brass and gold and silver, the work of the children of men, who have no knowledge and no breath.

5.14: And he killeth not, and giveth not life.
5.15: And he planteth not, and smiteth not.
5.18: He chastiseth not, and sheweth not mercy — but affliction is for the destruction of the perishing people of the Chaldeans.

6.10: And because of this the king was wroth, and was grieved, and commanded to bring them; and they brought them, and set them before him; and he said unto them: Cry out, and bow down unto my gods.
6.11: And they answered and said unto him: We will not obey thee in this matter, and we will not cry unto thy impure gods.
6.12: And he threatened them with much torment, and it availed not; for they had hardened their heart unto God.

6.19: And there is no other god besides Him, in heaven above and in earth beneath, who is able [over] all; and there is none who is like Him — who killeth and giveth life, who chastiseth and sheweth mercy.
6.20: And there is none who is delivered from His hand; for the King of heaven and earth is He.

6.24: And thou shalt be requited by the work of thy hands and by thy idols, until God shall thee, and bring thee down to the mouth of Gehenna; and He shall avenge thee because of all the transgression and sin which thou hast done upon the earth.
